# Add Second Region (us-west-2) to Crossplane Composition

To add us-west-2 without modifying existing claims, implement multi-region support at the **composition layer** using provider configs and resource expansion.

## Implementation

### 1. Define Provider Configurations

Create provider configs for both regions in your Crossplane namespace:

```yaml
---
# us-east-1 (primary region)
apiVersion: aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
kind: ProviderConfig
metadata:
  name: aws-useast1
spec:
  credentials:
    source: Secret
    secretRef:
      namespace: crossplane-system
      name: aws-credentials
      key: creds
  region: us-east-1

---
# us-west-2 (replication/secondary region)
apiVersion: aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
kind: ProviderConfig
metadata:
  name: aws-uswest2
spec:
  credentials:
    source: Secret
    secretRef:
      namespace: crossplane-system
      name: aws-credentials
      key: creds
  region: us-west-2
```

### 2. Extend Composition to Provision Multi-Region Resources

Update your `Composition` manifest to include us-west-2 resources. Keep the claim schema unchanged; the composition expands claims into region-specific managed resources.

**Key resources that span regions:**

```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.crossplane.io/v1
kind: Composition
metadata:
  name: web-app-composition
spec:
  compositeTypeRef:
    apiVersion: example.com/v1alpha1
    kind: WebApp
  resources:

    # ─── PRIMARY REGION (us-east-1) ───

    - name: s3-bucket-primary
      base:
        apiVersion: s3.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
        kind: Bucket
        metadata:
          name: app-bucket-primary
        spec:
          providerConfigRef:
            name: aws-useast1
          versioningConfiguration:
            status: Enabled
          serverSideEncryptionConfiguration:
            - ruleIndex: 0
              applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
                sseAlgorithm: AES256
          replicationConfiguration:
            role: !Sub "arn:aws:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/s3-replication-role"
            rules:
              - id: replicate-to-uswest2
                status: Enabled
                priority: 1
                destination:
                  bucket: arn:aws:s3:::app-bucket-replica
                  replicationTime:
                    status: Enabled
                    time:
                      minutes: 15
                filter:
                  prefix: ""

    - name: rds-instance
      base:
        apiVersion: rds.aws.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
        kind: DBInstance
        spec:
          providerConfigRef:
            name: aws-useast1
          dbInstanceIdentifier: app-db
          allocatedStorage: "20"
          engine: postgres
          engineVersion: "13.7"
          multiAZ: true  # Multi-AZ in primary region
          storageType: gp2
          deletionPolicy: Retain
          backupRetentionPeriod: 7
          publiclyAccessible: false
          # encryption & other security settings...

    - name: eks-cluster
      base:
        apiVersion: eks.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
        kind: Cluster
        spec:
          providerConfigRef:
            name: aws-useast1
          region: us-east-1
          name: app-cluster-useast1
          # version, role ARN, VPC config...

    # ─── SECONDARY REGION (us-west-2) ───

    - name: s3-bucket-replica
      base:
        apiVersion: s3.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
        kind: Bucket
        metadata:
          name: app-bucket-replica
        spec:
          providerConfigRef:
            name: aws-uswest2
          versioningConfiguration:
            status: Enabled
          serverSideEncryptionConfiguration:
            - ruleIndex: 0
              applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
                sseAlgorithm: AES256

    # Optional: Read-replica RDS in us-west-2 (if high availability needed)
    # - name: rds-read-replica
    #   base:
    #     apiVersion: rds.aws.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
    #     kind: DBInstance
    #     spec:
    #       providerConfigRef:
    #         name: aws-uswest2
    #       replicateSourceDBInstanceIdentifier: app-db
    #       ...
```

### 3. Create IAM Role for S3 Replication

Add to your IaC (outside Crossplane or via Crossplane IAM resources):

```yaml
apiVersion: iam.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: s3-replication-role
spec:
  assumeRolePolicyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [{
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Principal": {"Service": "s3.amazonaws.com"},
        "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"
      }]
    }
---
apiVersion: iam.aws.crossplane.io/v1beta1
kind: RolePolicyAttachment
metadata:
  name: s3-replication-policy
spec:
  roleName: s3-replication-role
  policyArn: arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonS3FullAccess
```

### 4. Apply Without Changing Claims

Users continue to submit the same claim unchanged:

```yaml
apiVersion: example.com/v1alpha1
kind: WebApp
metadata:
  name: my-app
spec:
  # Same spec as before—no region selection needed in claim
  environment: prod
  # Composition automatically provisions resources in us-east-1 (primary) 
  # and us-west-2 (replication target)
```

## Verification

After applying updated composition and provider configs:

```bash
# Check both provider configs are ready
kubectl get providerconfig -n crossplane-system

# Verify composition provisioned resources in both regions
kubectl get s3.aws.crossplane.io
kubectl get dbinstance.rds.aws.crossplane.io

# Confirm replication is active (via AWS console or CLI)
aws s3api get-bucket-replication --bucket app-bucket-primary --region us-east-1
```

## Environment Separation (dev/prod)

To separate dev/prod environments idiomatically, use **separate Compositions** per environment with distinct provider config references:

```yaml
# prod-composition.yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.crossplane.io/v1
kind: Composition
metadata:
  name: web-app-prod
spec:
  compositeTypeRef:
    apiVersion: example.com/v1alpha1
    kind: WebApp
  # Uses aws-useast1 and aws-uswest2 provider configs (prod credentials)

---
# dev-composition.yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.crossplane.io/v1
kind: Composition
metadata:
  name: web-app-dev
spec:
  compositeTypeRef:
    apiVersion: example.com/v1alpha1
    kind: WebApp
  # Uses aws-useast1-dev and aws-uswest2-dev provider configs (dev credentials)
```

Users select environment via `compositionRef` in the claim or `compositionSelector` labels—claims remain unchanged structurally.
